Executive summary

The catalog, product detail, cart, and dummy checkout work in Chromium desktop and mobile. Launch should not proceed with the declared cross-browser scope because Firefox and WebKit discard shipping-address input and block the critical checkout flow. The page also lacks a main landmark.

Verified readiness findings

Major QP-COMPAT-001

Shipping address input is unusable in Firefox and WebKit

core-flows · Firefox and WebKit desktop 1440x900

Reproduction

  1. Add two Wireless Mouse units to the cart.
  2. Proceed to the shipping-address step.
  3. Enter the published dummy name, street, city, state, and ZIP values.
  4. Attempt to save the address and continue to payment.

Expected

Address fields retain typed values and the payment form opens.

Actual

Every address field immediately returns to an empty value in Firefox and WebKit, so the modal remains on shipping and checkout cannot complete. WebKit also renders several fields at severely reduced widths.

Recommendation

Verify the controlled-input event handling and responsive form styles in Firefox/WebKit, then add a cross-browser checkout regression test.

Minor QP-A11Y-001

Primary e-commerce content has no main landmark

accessibility-smoke · Chromium desktop 1440x900

Reproduction

  1. Open the e-commerce practice page.
  2. Inspect the document landmarks and heading structure.

Expected

The primary storefront content is contained by exactly one main landmark.

Actual

The document contains a visible H1 but no main element or equivalent main landmark.

Recommendation

Wrap the page's primary e-commerce content in a main element while keeping the existing level-one heading.
